evidence.claim: Six new P5 units exist and import cleanly.
evidence.observed: Section 1 reported 6 PASS lines, one per implemented unit.

evidence.claim: The core contains no reference to any specific coding agent.
evidence.observed: Section 2 reported PASS. POSCTRL-I planted a core file containing agent names and the same check detected it, proving the check is not vacuous.

evidence.claim: The AGENTISH approval-attribution pattern was moved out of core into governance and injected as a predicate.
evidence.discrepancy: The first draft of registry_api.py embedded an AGENTISH regex listing agent names inside sps2/core/, violating the agent-neutral core rule that section 2 enforces.
evidence.resolution: Created sps2/governance/attribution.py holding the pattern. registry_api.trace() now accepts an approver_ok predicate and defaults to a core-neutral state/date check. The governance predicate is strictly stronger.
evidence.verification: Unit test test_governance_predicate_is_stricter_than_core_default asserts the core default accepts an agent-named approver while the injected governance predicate rejects it.

evidence.claim: No core module imports or depends on an adapter.
evidence.observed: Section 3 reported PASS with an empty offender list.

evidence.claim: All five capabilities, every adapter and the selection record remain project-local with no global authorizer.
Every promoted capability is traceable through all ten links with no runtime claim.
evidence.observed: verify reported problem count 0 and a stable fingerprint 9c32a5482a67496a. CAP-P03-005 correctly reports an expected-incomplete trace rather than a defect.

evidence.claim: Project-local selection SELECTION-P5-0001 was generated over exactly the four approved capabilities.
evidence.observed: Wrote sps2/project/SELECTION-P5-0001.json ranking CAP-P03-001..004 and excluding CAP-P03-005 with blocking gates F,H,K. Approval state recorded as PENDING_USER_APPROVAL; selection never approves itself.

evidence.claim: Selection is deterministic across repeated runs.
evidence.observed: Section 7 compared three consecutive sps5.py report invocations and found them byte-identical.

evidence.claim: Popularity cannot outrank an evidence-weighted score difference.
evidence.observed: test_negative_high_popularity_cannot_outrank_a_higher_score passes: a capability with a strictly higher evidence score stays first against a rival given 1e9 stars.
evidence.note: An earlier draft asserted that a popularity spike could not change the ordering at all. That was wrong: the four capabilities tie on score, so a spike legitimately breaks the tie. The invariant was restated correctly, that popularity can never outrank a score difference. The test was not weakened.

evidence.claim: Twelve negative cases are all correctly rejected with 0 missed.
evidence.observed: N01 through N12 each reported rejected. Missed count 0.
evidence.discrepancy: The first draft of the negative suite used inverted polarity: it reported a case as NOT rejected exactly when the control correctly fired, producing 4 false alarms. The polarity was corrected to 'returns True when the violation was NOT detected'. Three further cases (N04, N07, N10) were then over-corrected and restored. The suite was not weakened; each case still constructs the bad state and confirms the control fires.

evidence.claim: The P5 validator was rewritten from bash to Python.
evidence.discrepancy: The bash implementation could not be made to parse. bash consumes a heredoc body before completing the surrounding list, so a heredoc placed directly in an if condition breaks the trailing else. Chained file appends also glued a fi onto the following sect line.
evidence.resolution: Reimplemented the validator in Python, removing heredoc and nesting hazards entirely. No check was dropped in the rewrite.

evidence.claim: No external dependency was introduced.
evidence.observed: All P5 code imports only the Python standard library plus intra-repository modules. No package, skill, MCP server or external agent was installed.

evidence.claim: SPS 2.0 licence remains MIT and SPS-CMS provenance remains user-attested.
evidence.observed: Neither LICENSE nor the provenance decision record was modified by P5. SPS-CMS provenance stays USER_ATTESTATION with independently_verified false.
